title: CDBridge: A Cross-omics Post-training Bridge Strategy for Context-aware Biological Modeling
claim: A frozen-backbone, two-stage post-training bridge links long DNA sequence to context-specific protein function and expression through connected modules.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, bottom level brackets, top biological illustrations
description: A wide single-panel diagram. Along the top, illustrations show a chromosome, a protein database cylinder, tissue icons (brain, heart, lung) with colored histogram tracks for bulk RNA, and chains of beads for proteins and isoforms. Along the bottom, a left-to-right pipeline of colored boxes: a vertical DNA strip feeds a green trapezoid DNA Model (locked), then a red Multi-omics Connector (fire icon, trainable). The connector receives a Protein Model (locked) and a protein dictionary of colored squares. Next comes a blue Function Decoder, then a purple Conditional Decoder. The Conditional Decoder receives a green Single-cell Model (locked) and outputs a list of proteins with scores such as 0.9 and 0.3. A dashed red arrow links the top-right proteins to the output. Brackets labeled Gene, Function and Cell Level group the stages. Lock and flame icons mark frozen versus trained modules.
caption: Overview of the CDBridge framework for context-aware cross-omics modeling of the central dogma. CDBridge operates in two post-training stages built on frozen DNA and protein foundation models, which consists of two stages: (1) Seq-context learning, which identifies informative regions from long genomic sequences and maps them to protein-related functional representations. (2) Env-context learning, a conditional decoder that incorporates tissue embeddings to compose functional features into tissue-specific representations for gene expression prediction.
abstract: Linking genomic DNA to quantitative, context-specific expression remains a central challenge in computational biology. Current foundation models capture either tissue context or sequence features, but not both. Cross-omics systems, in turn, often overlook critical mechanisms such as alternative splicing and isoform reuse. We present CDBridge, a post-training strategy that unifies pretrained DNA and protein models into a context-aware framework without full retraining. CDBridge operates in two stages: (a) Seq-context learning, where a splicing-inspired token merge compresses long genomic regions into isoform-aware representations, and (b) Env-context learning, where a conditional decoder injects tissue embeddings to model expression under diverse biological contexts. To benchmark this setting, we introduce GTEx-Benchmark, derived from GTEx and Ensembl, which requires models to capture long-range exon dependencies, resolve isoform reuse, and predict tissue-specific expression levels. Across qualitative and quantitative tasks, CDBridge consistently outperforms prior methods that ignore central dogma constraints or context dependence, offering a scalable and biologically faithful solution for DNA-to-expression modeling.
